description: Mensuration is a branch of mathematics that deals with the measurement of geometric figures. It involves the calculation of length, area, and volume.

sections.title: 2D Shapes: Triangles and Quadrilaterals
sections.description: Basic formulas for the perimeter and area of plane figures.

key_concepts.explanation: The total length of the outer boundary of a 2D figure.
Half of the perimeter, primarily used in Heron's formula: s = (a+b+c)/2.

sections.title: 2D Shapes: Circles and Sectors
sections.description: Calculation of circumference and area for circular figures.

key_concepts.explanation: The diameter passes through the center and is always twice the length of the radius (d = 2r).

cases.condition: When the angle of the sector is 180 degrees

sections.title: 3D Shapes: Cube and Cuboid
sections.description: Formulas for the surface area and volume of three-dimensional figures.

key_concepts.explanation: The total three-dimensional space occupied by a solid figure.

steps.title: Finding the length of the longest rod
steps.detail: The length of the longest rod that can be placed perfectly inside a rectangular room is equal to the diagonal of that cuboid.

sections.title: 3D Shapes: Cylinder and Cone
sections.description: Analysis of measurements for 3D shapes with curved surfaces.

equations: Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2 * π * r * h
Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2 * π * r(r + h)
Curved Surface Area (CSA) = π * r * l
Total Surface Area (TSA) = π * r(r + l)

key_concepts.explanation: The distance from the apex of a cone straight down to a point on the circumference of its circular base.

results: Apply the Pythagoras theorem using the radius and height.

sections.title: 3D Shapes: Sphere and Hemisphere
sections.description: Properties and formulas of spherical shapes.

results: When a solid 3D shape is melted and recast into another solid shape, the total volume always remains exactly the same.
